Current guidance distinguishes alteration from rectification under the Land Registration Act 2002.
A suspected map mismatch is recorded as evidence for review and is not silently treated as corrected geometry.
The guide was last updated 1 June 2026.
Deed correction, register alteration and terrain-source correction remain separate evidence paths.
PG83 explains purposes for which the register may be altered under Schedule 4 to the Land Registration Act 2002.
Register-alteration authority does not create or validate elevation observations.
The product uses identifiable persistent features with feature lifecycles tied to real-world change.
Topographic feature identity is horizontal/contextual evidence, not a terrain-height measurement.
Real-world objects are represented in surveyed position where possible.
Generalised topographic geometry is not promoted to cadastral or exact parcel geometry.
GM_Point coordinates are easting/northing in metres in British National Grid.
Geometry-type conformance does not imply legal-boundary or elevation correctness.
Change-Only Update contains inserts, updates and departed features.
COU lineage must not be interpreted as a complete historical geometry archive.
The release-note index identifies current and previous releases and known-data-issue links.
FVDS validates holding completeness, not terrain height or legal boundary position.
TopographicArea represents polygon-based topographic objects.
TopographicArea polygons are contextual topography, not title polygons.
Available formats include GeoPackage, vector tiles and GML.
Supply cadence is freshness evidence and does not imply a specific feature changed.
Initial supply and Change-Only Update are distinct supply modes.
Cross-product synchronicity supports lineage only; it does not improve elevation accuracy.
The underlying Topography Layer database undergoes continuous revision.
Load date, extraction date and feature-version date must not be conflated.
Feature version date records when a new version was created.
Feature-version history is lineage evidence and is not a survey-date substitute.
OS OpenMap Local is designed as contextual street-level mapping.
Context mapping is not accepted as exact parcel geometry or elevation source.
OS Open TOID publishes persistent identifiers with a generalised location extracted from OS MasterMap products.
Open TOID locations are not used as parcel boundaries or raster sample points.
Point locations are rounded to the nearest metre.
Generalised Open TOID points are forbidden as exact sampling coordinates.
Open TOID includes identifiers from Topography, Sites and Highways feature types.
Identifier location is a join aid only and not a substitute for source geometry.
Sites Layer integrates with other OS MasterMap layers using common coordinate systems and identifiers.
Integration metadata does not establish legal site ownership extent or terrain elevation.
Sites Layer provides maintained extents for functional locations such as schools, hospitals and infrastructure sites.
Functional-site extent is not a registered-title boundary.
Sites Layer can be supplied nationally or in 5 km tiles.
Tile duplication/overlap behavior must not be interpreted as duplicate legal sites.
Functional sites are geolocated polygons representing collective function or activity.
Functional site polygons are excluded from cadastral parcel sampling.
Access points are captured as point features associated with a functional site.
Access points are navigation/context features and not exact parcel vertices.
The product is orthorectified aerial photography for general business use.
Imagery is visual/horizontal evidence and not the primary numeric terrain raster.
The imagery product is updated quarterly in February, May, August and November.
Image currency and appearance are separate from bare-earth height accuracy.
BHA is an enhancement to OS MasterMap Topography Layer for buildings and selected structures.
Building-height attribution is excluded from primary ground height-difference measurement.
BHA records the source TopographicArea TOID.
Process date and TOID version are lineage controls, not survey accuracy guarantees.
BHA is supplied as CSV and refreshed every six months.
Tile duplication must not be interpreted as multiple distinct buildings or measurements.
BHA is derived from and dependent on multiple other data sources.
Derived building heights are diagnostic/context only for this parcel terrain workflow.
Some Topography Layer building TOIDs can have no corresponding BHA value because of update-cycle differences or failed quality validation.
Missing BHA is not interpreted as zero building height or zero terrain difference.
BHA is derived from source DTM and DSM data.
One-decimal storage/derivation is not a parcel DTM accuracy guarantee.
BHA source DTMs represent bare ground while DSMs represent elevated surfaces.
BHA's building-footprint derivation is not substituted for parcel-wide EA DTM sampling.
CQL2 1.0.0 is an official OGC implementation standard.
Filter grammar conformance does not validate the geometry or elevation values returned.
Part 3 extends OGC API Features with enhanced filtering using CQL2.
Filtering must be explicit and reproducible; selected features are not assumed numerically correct solely because the filter is valid.
